title: One declaration of triage-decision.json's wire shape — three readers of dropped[] and two meanings of skip_shipped drift today
summary: F30 architecture review M2. triage-decision.json is parsed by committedset (Committed/DecisionTopN/Deferred, and since F30 DispositionsFrom), inboxmover (CommittedIDs: top_n ∪ skip_shipped as the WORKED set; DeferredIDs; ClosedDroppedIDs: close-class drops), and core/carryover (triageDroppedIDs, reason-blind). skip_shipped is 'committed' to inboxmover.CommittedIDs but an 'answer, not committed' to DispositionsFrom. The import cycle that justified the copies no longer binds: committedset is a stdlib-only leaf.
fix: Declare the decision document ONCE in committedset — Decision{TopN, Deferred, Dropped{ID,Reason}, SkipShipped{TaskID,GitSHA}, SkipRejected{TaskID}, EscalateBlock{TaskID,Reason,FailCount}} — and make Dispositions, ClosedDroppedIDs, triageDroppedIDs and CommittedIDs (renamed for what it is: the set that rides the landing) projections of it.
acceptance: Exactly one non-test declaration of the dropped[] / skip_shipped[] wire tags (a single-declaration pin like cycleoutcome's TestLaneScopeProjection_SingleWireShapeDeclaration)
Each projection keeps its policy byte-for-byte (existing tests stay green unchanged)
